title: Declared test commands are never recognized from Codex sessions on Windows: Codex's quoted absolute pwsh wrapper fails the wrapper rule
outcome: The declared route recognizes Codex's ordinary double-quoted absolute Windows pwsh executable wrapper while preserving the existing inner-line rules and direct command behavior; arbitrary or ambiguous wrappers remain refused.
acceptance: From source (the declared route's wrapper parsing) and a reproduction, show that Codex's Windows exec envelope `"<absolute path>\pwsh.exe" -Command '<line>'` (a double-quoted absolute path containing spaces and backslashes) is what the wrapper rule rejects today.

The declared route accepts exactly that envelope: a double-quoted absolute Windows path whose final component is pwsh.exe, then -Command (or -c, with any of -NoProfile, -NonInteractive, -NoLogo before it, as for bare pwsh), then one single-quoted script word, which is judged by the existing line rules unchanged. A Windows-shaped positive test drives a Codex-shaped declared PASS through the recognizer.

Negative tests show these are still refused: a quoted powershell.exe, cmd.exe or any other executable; a quoted relative path; a quoted path not ending in pwsh.exe; other or extra options; a script that isn't one single-quoted word; mixed quoting. Direct (unwrapped) declared-command behaviour and the existing declared tests are unchanged.
The maintained full gate passes on the exact committed tree with a credited host record, and the Codex/Claude review pair has no outstanding Medium or higher.
